glosses: to quake (of a building or the earth)
to tremble, shake (of a person)
содрогаться, сотрясаться; (за)дрожать, вздрагивать
Trembler.

examples.text: Meine Welt erzittert. Ich begreife nicht, was um mich herum geschieht, aber mein Bett erbebt, die Bücherregale an den Wänden geraten ins Wanken, brechen schließlich in sich zusammen.
examples.translation: Mon monde tressaille. Je ne comprends pas ce qui se passe autour de moi mais mon lit tremble, les étagères de livres se mettent à chanceler et finissent par s’effondrer.

glosses: durch die Bewegung der Erde in Bewegung versetzt werden, sich bewegen

examples.text: Durch die vorbeifahrenden Panzer erbebten die umliegenden Gebäude und die Fensterscheiben klirrten.
„Während die Männer eilends durch den Wald brachen, entstand ein gewaltiges Getöse ‚ein solches Prasseln und Brausen, daß die Erde erbebte und der Wald zu brüllen schien‘.“

glosses: so von einem Gefühl übermannt werden, dass der Körper leicht zittert

examples.text: „Vor jedem raschen Laut, Vor jedem Tropfen, der vom Zweige niederthaut, Erbebt sie scheu mit mädchenhaftem Zagen.“ (1818)
„Die von Abbas N. Sayars beschriebene Figur Müslim erhält einen Brief von seiner jungen Frau Halime und erbebt beim Lesen.“

translations.source_sense_description: durch die Bewegung der Erde in Bewegung versetzt werden, auch über die Erde selbst: sich bewegen

glosses: A trembling or shaking.

examples.text: We felt a quake in the apartment every time the train went by.

glosses: An earthquake, a trembling of the ground with force.

examples.text: California is plagued by quakes; there are a few minor ones almost every month.

Well, everybody talks about the California quakes
But the first time I ever felt the earth shake
Was in Miami, when Amy touched me.

glosses: Something devastating, like a strong earthquake.

examples.text: But HS1 was more exposed to the COVID quake than most given its inherent reliance on international travel, which had collapsed, leaving cross-Channel operator Eurostar stacked with millions of debt.

glosses: To tremble or shake.

examples.text: I felt the ground quaking beneath my feet.
Dorus threw Pamela behind a tree; where she stood quaking like the partridge on which the hawk is even ready to seize.
The mountains quake at him, and the hills melt, and the earth is burnt at his presence.

glosses: To be in a state of fear, shock, amazement, etc., such as might cause one to tremble.

examples.text: Turning back, then, toward the basement staircase, she began to grope her way through blinding darkness, but had taken only a few uncertain steps when, of a sudden, she stopped short and for a little stood like a stricken thing, quite motionless save that she quaked to her very marrow in the grasp of a great and enervating fear.
If Cupid have not spent all his quiver in / Venice, thou wilt quake for this shortly.
Now could I drink hot blood / And do such bitter business as the bitter day / Would quake to look on.
Who honours not his father, Henry the fifth, that made all France to quake, Shake he his weapon at us, and pass by.
Son of man, eat thy bread with quaking, and drink thy water with trembling and carefulness.

glosses: ритор. волноваться, испытывать потрясение

glosses: To shake nervously, often from fear or horror.

examples.text: On seeing the spider under his pillow, John shuddered.
VVreath'd vp in fatall folds iuſt in his way, / The feare where of doth make him ſhake, & ſhudder, […]
What makes me shudder so? / I shudder and I sigh to think / That even Cicero / And many-minded Homer were / Mad as the mist and snow.

glosses: To vibrate jerkily.
A shivering tremor, often from fear or horror.

examples.text: Seeing the spider under his pillow gave John a shudder.

glosses: A moment of almost pleasurable fear; a frisson.

examples.text: They name thee before me, / ⁠A knell to mine ear; / A shudder comes o'er me— / ⁠Why wert thou so dear?
… and was not that slight tremble, a shudder which went through her young body, when his kiss, glowing and scorching with his wild passion, had dared to touch her tiny ice-cold hand?
